adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` evaluates to the literal key `"[object Object]"` (overwritten by the identical key on line 10), so the credential-sharing "minimum token response" validation asserts only `access_token: z.string()` and silently accepts any malformed sync-endpoint payload — a validator that verifies nothing while reading as if it does.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, the `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined as `z.object({ access_token: z.string(), [z.string().toString()]: z.number(), [z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional() })`. In a JS/TS object literal, computed property keys are evaluated immediately to a single string key. `z.string()` returns an object, so `.toString()` yields a fixed string (e.g. `"[object Object]"` or a similar constant), meaning these are not wildcard/index-signature validations. Additionally, both computed keys evaluate to the same string and the latter overwrites the former, leaving no enforced numeric expiry field at all. As a result, when credential sharing is enabled, `safeParse` effectively only requires `access_token` and does not validate an expiry as the code/comments imply, allowing malformed sync-endpoint payloads through.
